ingredients.item: pork belly, skin off, cut into slabs 1 cm thick
ingredients.preparation: slightly thinner than the classic — the paste wants faster cooking

ingredients.item: Lettuce and perilla ssam, ssamjang thinned with a splash of water for dipping, kimchi , steamed rice , garlic coins and green chili slices

instructions.heading: Step 1
instructions.action: Slabs on the pan in a single layer, medium-low. The first minutes are quiet rendering again — the paste darkens one shade at the edges and the fat begins to gloss the pan. Turn every 90 seconds.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the paste should deepen toward brick and smell toasted-chile-sweet, not burnt. Any black edges on the first turn mean the flame is a notch high — lower it and the batch is fine.

instructions.heading: Step 2
instructions.action: At 12–14 minutes, scissors into bite pieces directly on the pan, toss in the hot fat 60 seconds for the crisp lacquered faces, and pull to the platter.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: test piece: crisp lacquered edge, the three-layer belly interior, then the paste's ferment-heat arriving after the fat. If the heat lands before the pork, the film was thick — thinner next batch.

instructions.heading: Step 3
instructions.action: Ssam sequence as the classic: leaf, thin ssamjang swipe, hot pork piece, garlic or chili, fold, one bite. Rice and kimchi between.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: the ssam test should read as the classic's rich cousin — same crisp, same fat, a red edge on the flavor — not as a sweet-spicy pork candy. When in doubt, thin the paste further; the pork is the headline.

storageNotes: Painted slabs hold 24 hours refrigerated (the curing clock is running). Cooked, 3 days; dice into fried rice or fold into a lunchbox gimbap-style roll.
Variations: the undressed classic (#M10) is the parent; a spoon of the paste into the ssamjang dip instead of onto the meat splits the difference; kimchi beside the slabs on the pan, same as ever.
